scenarios.label: Likely Eligible
scenarios.description: A patient who meets all inclusion criteria and triggers no exclusion criteria.

scenarios.label: Likely Ineligible
scenarios.description: A patient who otherwise qualifies but is currently taking insulin, a high-impact exclusion criterion that quickly disqualifies them if asked early.
scenarios.earlyStopNote: Screening can end as soon as EXC-004 is answered 'Yes, taking insulin'; remaining questions are optional for the recruiter.

scenarios.label: Likely Ineligible (AI-assisted early stop via age range)
scenarios.description: A patient below the protocol's minimum age. The age question (DEM-002/DEM-001 depending on generated order, linked to INC-001, a Required numeric-range criterion) is marked canTriggerEarlyStop, so the recorded answer is sent to Claude to interpret against the '18 to 75' range rather than relying on the yes/no heuristic, which cannot evaluate numeric ranges.

sampleAnswers.notes: Below the required 18-75 range; AI-assisted evaluation classifies this as failed with reasoning referencing the range.

scenarios.earlyStopNote: As soon as the age question is answered '16', the answers endpoint returns earlyStopRecommended=true with a reason referencing criterion INC-001. The session stays InProgress and next-question keeps working; the recruiter chooses End & View Summary (POST /{sessionId}/end) or Continue Screening. In fallback mode (Claude unavailable) this specific numeric-range case is NOT caught by the deterministic yes/no heuristic — a documented limitation, see README.md/CODESETUP.md hackathon simplifications.

scenarios.label: Sex-Specific Question Filtering (male patient)
scenarios.description: A male patient. The 'What sex were you assigned at birth?' demographic question (DEM-SEX) is asked first because EXC-002 (pregnancy) is tagged appliesToSex: Female; answering 'Male' means EXC-002 resolves to not_applicable and its dedicated question is never shown.

sampleAnswers.notes: Triggers EXC-002 (pregnancy) to resolve as not_applicable; that question is never asked.

scenarios.notApplicableNote: EXC-002 (pregnancy/breastfeeding) resolves to not_applicable and is listed separately in the summary under 'Not applicable to this patient' — never under missing/skipped information. As in Scenario 1, HbA1c/insulin/kidney are requiresClinicalReview criteria, so the overall recommendation still lands on Needs Clinical Review rather than Likely Eligible.

scenarios.label: Needs Clinical Review
scenarios.description: A patient who is uncertain about their current diabetes medications, so a medication-related exclusion criterion cannot be confidently resolved.

sampleAnswers.response: Not sure / unsure of current medications
sampleAnswers.notes: Missing/uncertain medication history triggers clinical review.
